settle: Inspector identifiers (not published) would separate inspector stringency from place; the NTA effect would then be decomposed into inspector and restaurant parts. Restaurant size, seats and age of premises would test whether the raw differences are restaurant mix.

research_needed.question: Do individual NYC inspectors differ in stringency, as Jones 2004 found in Tennessee?
research_needed.data: DOHMH inspection records with inspector id (FOIL)
research_needed.design: inspector fixed effects with rotation as quasi-random assignment

research_needed.question: Do hearings dismiss violations at different rates by neighbourhood?

notes: Raw critical violations per initial inspection range from 1.65 (Midtown-Times Square) to 2.37 (Chinatown-Two Bridges); unadjusted, the permutation statistic is 4.2 times its null mean (p < 0.001). Restaurant count alone brings it to 2.6, cuisine alone to 2.4, and the registered set to 1.11. The registered adjustment set accounts for the raw differences; the share due to each covariate was not separated further. Exploratory, not registered (its result was seen during a synthetic-outcome check of the script): routine initial inspections per restaurant-year, adjusted for first score band, cuisine, chain, restaurant count and new status, give p = 0.015 and tau = 0.016, detectable but small (adjusted rate ratios 0.95 to 1.08). Also exploratory: all cycle inspections with stage as covariate, p = 0.026. Fixed source is the Underlay snapshot because the live table drops closed restaurants and revises recent violations (docs/underlay_drift.md).
notes_referee: Referee p 0.323. Contested stands under rule 1, but refutes only place effects of ~5%+ (SD ~0.05 at 80% power); centred SD 0.024. Restaurant-count covariate alone moves p 0.008 -> 0.32, absorbing a density gradient (~3.5%, r = -0.51).
